summary: Vehicular-combat spy-driving series beginning with Bally Midway's 1983 arcade original and later continuing through console reboots.

entries.title: Spy Hunter

emulation.notes: Use the original arcade set and map the yoke, gear shift, pedal, and weapon buttons carefully.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade-accurate emulation with modern display scaling

primary.why: Spy Hunter was designed for Bally Midway's arcade hardware with a yoke, gear shift, pedal, and dedicated weapon buttons; the home ports and later compilations are useful access routes but do not replace the original cabinet design.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME or on original hardware; Midway Arcade Origins on PlayStation 3/Xbox 360 is a convenient legal compilation route if owned.

entries.remaster_caveats: Later compilation releases are access routes for the arcade game, not remasters with new content.

entries.title: Spy Hunter II

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation for the split-screen cabinet original.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade-accurate emulation with modern display scaling

primary.why: Spy Hunter II was released only as an arcade game in its original era, with a behind-the-car perspective and cooperative split-screen cabinet design; later appearances are compilation routes.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME or original hardware; Midway Arcade Origins on PlayStation 3/Xbox 360 is the easiest compilation route if owned.

entries.remaster_caveats: No contemporary home ports; compilation releases preserve the arcade game.

entries.title: Super Spy Hunter

emulation.notes: Use accurate NES emulation for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Accurate NES output with modern scaling

primary.why: Super Spy Hunter began as Sunsoft's Battle Formula in Japan and was released in North America as a Spy Hunter-branded NES sequel; the NES game is the original playable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the NES version in Mesen, Nestopia UE, MiSTer, or original hardware.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Japanese title Battle Formula was localized as Super Spy Hunter in North America.

entries.title: SpyHunter

emulation.notes: Use PS2 emulation for higher internal resolution while preserving the original console version.

primary.why: SpyHunter launched on PlayStation 2 before later GameCube, Xbox, handheld, PC, Mac OS X, and Zodiac versions. The PS2 release was the best-received route, while the PC port had compromised graphics and controls.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation 2 version in PCSX2 with high internal resolution, widescreen only if verified stable, or on original hardware.

entries.remaster_caveats: This 2001 reboot/sequel is distinct from the 1983 arcade game and the 2012 reboot.

entries.title: SpyHunter 2

emulation.notes: Use xemu for the Xbox primary when compatibility is acceptable; use PCSX2 as a practical fallback.

primary.why: SpyHunter 2 released for PlayStation 2 and Xbox with no sourced platform-exclusive content. The Xbox route has the stronger console hardware ceiling while preserving the same game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version in xemu where compatible, or use original Xbox hardware; PS2 via PCSX2 is the fallback if compatibility is better.

entries.remaster_caveats: Sequel to the 2001 reboot, not the 1987 arcade Spy Hunter II.

entries.title: SpyHunter: Nowhere to Run

emulation.notes: Use native Windows where possible; Xbox or PS2 emulation are fallbacks.

primary.why: Nowhere to Run released on PlayStation 2 and Xbox in 2006, then received a Windows version in 2009. Windows provides the highest output ceiling and the same sourced game content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a compatibility setup; use Xbox or PS2 emulation only if the PC release is unavailable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Film tie-in origin became a stand-alone game; it is the series entry with on-foot play as well as vehicle sequences.

entries.title: Spy Hunter

emulation.notes: Use real Vita hardware for the primary route; Vita3K compatibility should be checked before committing to emulation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native Vita output or emulator scaling where compatible

primary.why: The 2012 Spy Hunter reboot released for PlayStation Vita and Nintendo 3DS. The Vita version is the higher-fidelity handheld route, with no sourced 3DS-exclusive content.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation Vita hardware; use Nintendo 3DS only for platform preference.

entries.remaster_caveats: Second reboot of the series, distinct from the 1983 arcade game and 2001 SpyHunter.
